Date: 2026-10-03 09:12 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing & short extension — PineScale POC

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about Redwood latency and the embed pipeline. We burned through the initial timebox faster than expected due to an expanded test matrix and a couple of surprising inference-heavy prompts.

Two asks:
- Can we get a two-week extension to the POC (same environment) so our data science team can finish the integration tests?
- If we need more runtime beyond that, can Redwood provide a short-term overage pricing or convert unused days to credits toward a reserved commitment?

We're sensitive to budget here. If there is a simple, low-friction option (flat extension fee or a credit conversion), that would help our procurement team move faster.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call.

— Evan
VP Product, PineScale
Evan.Wu@pinescale.ai
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Wu <evan.wu@pinescale.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03 13:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & short extension — PineScale POC

Evan — great to hear, and glad the tests are progressing. Short answer: yes, we have two straightforward paths we typically offer for shortpilot extensions. I'm attaching a usage estimate and a draft mutual action plan so you can see the options side-by-side.

Option A — Timebox extension (14 days): flat extension fee of $4,200 to preserve the current environment and priority routing. No changes to ratecard during extension.

Option B — Credit conversion + capped overage: convert up to 25% of unused days into a voucher (applies automatically to the next 90 days) or we can bill overage at our day-rate with a 12% concession if you commit to a 3-month reserved tier within 30 days.

I know finance and procurement care about low-friction docs. If you like Option B, we can prepare a short addendum that includes the credit conversion logic and a DocuSign wrapper for partner-friendly approval.

Proposed next step: 20-minute sync tomorrow to pick option and confirm a DocuSign flow.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Subject: Internal: PineScale extension concession request (DEAL-PS-439)

Hi Ben/Laura — Evan from PineScale asked for a 2-week extension; they are uneasy about budget and prefer either a small flat fee or a way to convert unused days into credits. Attached are the usage estimate and my notes from the call.

My recommendation is to offer Option B (credit conversion + capped overage) as our primary. Suggested commercial terms:
- 14-day extension at $0 (no upfront fee) contingent on:
  - conversion of up to 25% unused days into a voucher valid for 90 days
  - a conditional 12% concession on overage rates if they convert to a 3-month reserved tier within 30 days after the pilot
- Cap on total concession exposure at $6,000 for this customer (finance-friendly)

Reasons: preserves momentum, reduces procurement friction, and gives us a clear path to conversion. Tradeoffs: slightly higher short-term exposure vs. a flat fee which might slow procurement.

Ask: Ben — can you approve the 12% concession + $6k cap? Laura — any flags from billing/legal on voucher wording? Stephanie — ops considerations on preserving the env for free for two weeks?

Thanks,
Chloe
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 11:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: PineScale extension concession request (DEAL-PS-439)

Chloe — sounds reasonable. Approve the conditional concession but tighten the cap language: 12% concession on overage as you proposed, with a hard cap of $5,500 (we should keep a small buffer). Require a signed addendum before the extension is applied.

Laura — confirm that the voucher language limits redemptions to inference/hosting credits only (no professional services). If legal signs off we'll route the addendum via DocuSign.

Stephanie — ops: can you confirm we can keep the same GPU pool and priority routing for 14 days without impacting scheduled capacity? If not, we switch to a lower-priority pool and note that in the addendum.

If everyone is OK, Chloe: prepare the addendum with DocuSign link and I'll send a short email to Evan with a one-line commercial summary and the signature request.

— Ben

Evan — thanks for your patience. Quick update and final offer from Redwood:

Agreed path (final):
- 14-day extension starting when DocuSign is complete.
- No upfront extension fee.
- PineScale will receive a voucher equal to 25% of current unused pilot days; voucher valid for 90 days and redeemable for inference credits only (cannot be applied to professional services).
- If PineScale signs a 3-month reserved commitment within 30 days after the extension, Redwood will apply a 12% concession to any overage billed during the extension period (capped at $5,500).

Attachments: Pilot_Addendum_Draft.docx (addendum prepared), PineScale_MutualActionPlan_v2.pdf, POC-Usage-Estimate.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Evan — review addendum and sign via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/embedded/abc123-addendum
2) Once signed, we'll schedule the 14-day environment hold and share a calendar invite for the handoff call.

If you want to discuss, Ben and I are available tomorrow morning for a quick call.

Best,
